line: Framework Laptop 16 (2025, AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series, DIY Edition)
config_name: Laptop 16 DIY — Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 32GB DDR5 (2x16GB), 1TB NVMe, RTX 5070 8GB Expansion Bay Graphics Module

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (12-core/24-thread Zen 5/5c, up to 5.1GHz)
specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 8GB GDDR7 (swappable Expansion Bay module) + Radeon 890M iGPU
specs.gpu_notes: Configurator verbatim: "Slide the Graphics Module in for a massive boost in gaming, creation, and simulation performance. Configured with 8GB of GDDR7"; "Increases the thickness of the rear section to 21.95mm"
specs.ports: 6x user-swappable Expansion Card slots + Expansion Bay (RTX 5070 module), 3.5mm
specs.os: None (DIY — bring your own; Windows or Linux; CUDA works on Linux + Windows)

battery.notes: 85Wh. dGPU module costs ~1-1.5h vs shell config; users report ~6-7.5h light use with module installed.

price.notes: Configurator sum (2026-11-24): AI 9 HX 370 base $2,608 + 32GB +$750 (assumed same as FW13) + 1TB +$300 + RTX 5070 8GB module (~$1,200 est.; module adder price was truncated by batch-noise in configurator fetch — flagged estimated). Excludes 6 expansion cards + OS. Pre-order batches mostly sold out.

reviews.quote: first laptop ever to earn a 10/10 repairability score

praises: The only laptop whose GPU is a slide-in module you can replace in seconds — future-proof gaming in a repairable chassis
RTX 5070 module brings real DLSS gaming and CUDA acceleration to an otherwise iGPU machine
Module is shareable across FW16 owners and upgradeable to the next GPU generation without buying a new laptop
HX 370 + 32GB socketed RAM + dual M.2 = a genuinely serviceable creator/gaming desktop-replacement
165Hz matte panel and 6-speaker system with subwoofer are big upgrades over FW13
complaints: GPU module sold out in nearly every batch — the headline feature is the scarcest item
Module adds weight and thickness ("Increases the thickness of the rear section to 21.95mm") — ~2.5kg total
dGPU module costs ~$1,200 CAD on top, pushing the total near flagship gaming-laptop money
8GB VRAM on the module limits the newest AAA titles at 1600p+ ultra
Battery drops ~1-1.5h with the module installed even when idle

design_philosophy: Framework's most radical expression: a laptop where even the GPU is a modular, generational upgrade rather than a fixed spec. This top FW16 tier is a buy-once-upgrade-forever desktop replacement — the RTX 5070 slides out when the next module ships, and everything else in the machine remains a documented, orderable spare part.
standouts: Only laptop with a user-replaceable, generationally upgradeable discrete GPU
iFixit 10/10 repairability platform with CUDA-capable dGPU — rare combo for local ML tinkering
dealbreakers: Pre-order batch system: effectively sold out with December+/Q1 ship dates — cannot buy today
~$4,900 CAD all-in approaches custom-desktop territory for an 8GB-VRAM module
